rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be an appositive to أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم or آيَةٍ, an object of an omitted أعني, or a predicate of omitted هي.
rows.anchor: أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير بدل من قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi reads إني with initial hamza kasra, treating it as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ( إني ) بكسر الهمزة على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here creating means shaping and bringing something forth to a measured form, not originating it from nothing; the verse names its material and shape.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخلق التصويلا والإبراز على مقدار معين لا اليجاد من العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes هيئة as a verbal noun meaning what is prepared, as خلق can mean the created thing.
rows.anchor: والهيئة مصدر بمعنى المهيأ كالخلق بمعنى المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes هيئة a noun for a state or thing rather than a verbal noun; the verbal nouns are الهئ and التهيؤ, and هيئة is substance on one analysis, an accident on the other.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها اسم الحال الشئ وليست مصدرا وإنما المصدر الهئ والتهيؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هيئة is explained as a quality formed when one or more boundaries surround a body.
rows.anchor: من إحاطة الحد الواحد أو الحدود بالجسم والمعنى أني أقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isa forms from clay, to win belief and repel denial, something prepared like a bird or a form resembling one.
rows.anchor: أني أقدر لاجل تحصيل إيمانكم ودفع تكذيبكم إياي من الطين شيئا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats the kaf as a noun, either an object of أخلق or an adjective of an omitted object.
rows.anchor: والكاف إنا اسم كما ذهب اليه أبو الحسن في موضع نصب على المفعولية لأخلق

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority treat the kaf as a particle attached to an omitted phrase that itself modifies the omitted object.
rows.anchor: وإما حرف كما ذهب اليه الجمهور فتتعلق بمحذوف وقع نعتا ايضا

rows.speaker: يزيد وحمزة
rows.claim: Yazid and Hamza read كهيئة with a doubled ya.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد وحمزة كهيئة بتشديد الياء

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim relays Khalaf's report that Hamza drops the hamza and gives the ya its vowel.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن القاسم يقول : بلغني أن خلفا يقول

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
rows.claim: The people of Medina and Yaqub read الطائر; al-Alusi notes the same reading in al-Maida.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب الطائر ومثله في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فيه returns to the implied هيئة in the sense of the prepared thing, since an abstract quality cannot receive a breath.
rows.anchor: الضمير للهيئة المقدرة في نظم الكلام لكن بمعنى الشئ المهيأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is masculine here by reference to the thing's meaning, while al-Maida uses feminine agreement with the word هيئة; the shift is clear of ambiguity.
rows.anchor: وذكر الضمير هنا مراعاة للمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the pronoun to refer to the kaf as a noun, which in reality means the thing it describes.
rows.anchor: وقع في كلام غير واحد كون الضمير للكاف بناءا على أنها اسم

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham objects that treating the pronoun as referring to the kaf noun would predict an unattested expression like مررت بكالأسد.
rows.anchor: واعترضه ابن هشام بأنه لو كان كما زعموا لسمع في الكلام مررت بكالاسد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others object that referring a pronoun back to the kaf is unfamiliar.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم بأن عود الضمير إليها غير معهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result is a living, flying bird like other birds.
rows.anchor: فيكون طيرا ( حيا طيارا كسائر الطيور

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaddal reads the verb with feminine agreement, فتكون.
rows.anchor: وقرأ المفضل فتكون بتاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: يعقوب وأبو جعفر ونافع
rows.claim: Yaqub, Abu Jaafar, and Nafi read طائرا instead of طيرا.
rows.anchor: ويعقوب وأبو جعفر ونافع طائرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may modify يكون or طيرا and means by God's command; life-giving is God's act, with the breath as its occasion, not a special property of Isa or Gabriel's spirit.
rows.anchor: والمراد بأمر الله واشار بذلك إلى أن إحياءه من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could bring life through anyone's breath if He willed, without resistance or failure.
rows.anchor: بل لو شاء الله تعالى الإحياء بنفخ أي شخص كان لكان من غير تخلف ولا استعصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bird miracle suits Isa's own creation without a father.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه المعجزة مناسبة لخلقه من غير أب

rows.speaker: المعظم
rows.claim: The majority say the Israelites demanded the miracle obstinately, asking Isa to make a bat; after he did so, they called him a magician.
rows.anchor: فذهب المعظم إلى الاول قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They singled out the bat as a highly complete sign of divine power: it has teeth, bears young, flies without feathers, has ears and milk-producing breasts, laughs, and sees only at twilight.
rows.anchor: لانه أكمل الطير خلقا وأبلغ دلالة على القدرة لأن له نابا واسنانا ويحيض ويلد ويطير بغير ريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commonly held view is that Isa made no bird other than a bat.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Ibn Abbas the report that Isa's bird was a bat.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه أبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while people watched and fell dead once out of sight, distinguishing it from God's unmediated creation.
rows.anchor: قال وهب : كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون اليه فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Isa made several kinds of birds.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خلق أنواعا من الطير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold the miracle was not requested; Ibn Ishaq's report has Isa offer to make a bird to schoolboys, who doubt he can, then he shapes and breathes into clay and it flies from his hands.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى الثاني فقد أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن إسحق ان عيسى عليع السلام

rows.speaker: ابن إسحق
rows.claim: In Ibn Ishaq's account, the boys carry news of the flying bird to their teacher and spread the story among people.
rows.anchor: فذكروه لمعلمهم وأفشوه في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأبرئ is coordinated with أخلق and falls under the scope of أني.
rows.anchor: الأكمة ( عطف على ( أخلق ) فهو داخل في حيز ( أني )

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak's transmission from Ibn Abbas defines al-akmah as one born blind.
rows.anchor: هو الذي ولد اعمى أخرجه ابن جرير من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas describes al-akmah as one whose eye was wiped flat, whose sight did not open, and who was created without an eyeball.
rows.anchor: أنه الممسوح العين الذي لم يشق بصره ولم يخلق له حدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the only person in the early Muslim community with al-akmah in this sense was Qatada ibn Diama al-Sadusi.
rows.anchor: قيل : ولم يكن في صدر هذه الأمة أكمة بهذا المعنى غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid defines al-akmah as someone who sees by day but not by night.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنه الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets al-akmah as a person with weak or dim eyesight.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنه الأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means that Isa cures blindness, removing al-akmah from its condition.
rows.anchor: أي أخلص ( الأكمه ) من الكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-abras is someone with the familiar skin disease al-wadah.
rows.anchor: والأبرص ( وهو الذي به الوضح المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two ailments are singled out because they were difficult cases that defeated even the numerous, highly skilled physicians of Isa's time.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص هذين الأمرين لأنهما أمران معضلان أعجزا الاطباء وكانوا في غاية الحذاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God matched each people with a miracle in the field where their expertise lay: medicine for Isa's people, magic for Moses' people, and eloquence for the Arabs.
rows.anchor: ولهذا أراهم الله تعالى المعجزة من جنس الطب كما أرى قوم موسى عليه السلام المعجزة بالعصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning these cures does not rule out Isa curing other conditions; reports describe additional healings.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار على هذين الأمرين لا يدل على نفي ما عداهما لقد روى أنه عليه السلام أبرأ أيضا غيرهما

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says as many as fifty thousand sick people might gather for Isa; those able to reach him came, and he went to those unable to do so, treating them through prayer to God on condition of faith.
rows.anchor: وروى عن وهب أنه ربما اجتمع على عيسى عليه السلام من المرضى خمسون ألفا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Isa's prayer addressed God as lord, mighty one, and king of heaven and earth, affirming His power and asking by His noble name and luminous face.
rows.anchor: وكان دعاؤه الذي يدعو به للمرضى والزمنى والعميان والمجانين وغيرهم اللهم أنت إله من في السماء

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says reciting the prayer over a frightened or mentally ill person, or writing it and giving it to drink, can benefit them, God willing.
rows.anchor: ومن خواص هذا الدعاء كما قال وهب أنه إذا قرئ على الفزع والمجنون وكتب له وسقى منه نفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the predicate of أني.
rows.anchor: عطف على خبر ( أني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission qualifier marks this extraordinary act as God's work and guards against supposing its agent divine, since reviving the dead is unlike ordinary human acts.
rows.anchor: وقيد الإحياء بالإذن كما فعل في الأول لأنه عظيم يكاد يتوهم منه ألوهية فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Isa revived the dead through the prayer يا حي يا قيوم.
rows.anchor: وكان إحياؤه بالدعاء وكان دعاؤه يا حي ياقيوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says he prayed two units, reciting al-Mulk and al-Sajda, praised God, then invoked seven names before reviving the dead.
rows.anchor: كان إذا أراد أن يحي الموتى صلى ركعتين يقرأ في الأول تبارك الذي بيده الملك وفي الثانية تنزيل السجدة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi judges the report about the two prayers and seven names not strong.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي : ليس بالقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Isa struck the dead person, grave, or skull with his staff; the person revived by God's permission, spoke, then soon died again.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه كان إذا أراد أن يحي ميتا ضرب بعصاه الميت أو القبر أو الجمجمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna transmits from Ibn Abbas that Isa revived four people: Azar, a widow's son, a tax collector's daughter, and Sam son of Noah.
rows.anchor: وأخرج محي السنة عن ابن عباس أنه قال : قد أحيا عليه السلام أربعة أنفس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Azar was Isa's friend; his sister sent word after he had been dead three days, and Isa prayed at his grave, whereupon he rose, lived for some time, and had a child.
rows.anchor: فوجدوه قد مات منذ ثلاثة أيام فقال لاخته : انطلقي بنا إلى قبره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, Isa revived a widow's son during his funeral procession; he sat up, came down from the bearers, carried the bier home, then lived and had a child.
rows.anchor: فمر به ميتا على عيسى عليه السلام على سرير يحمل فدعا الله تعالى عيسى فجلس على سريره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The tax collector's daughter had died the previous day; Isa prayed for her, she revived, lived for some time, and had a child.
rows.anchor: ماتت له بنت بالأمس فدعا الله تعالى واحياها وبقيت زمانا وولد لها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sam son of Noah emerged from his grave after Isa invoked God's greatest name; half his hair had turned gray from fear of the Hour, and he asked whether it had come.
rows.anchor: فخرج من قبره وقد شاب نصف رأسه خوفا من قيام الساعة ولم يكونوا يشيبون في ذلك الزمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Isa told Sam the Hour had not come, Sam agreed to die only if God protected him from death's agonies; Isa prayed and this was granted.
rows.anchor: قال : بشرط أن يعيذني الله تعالى من سكرات الموت فدعا الله تعالى له ففعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports say the Jews had argued Isa revived only the recently dead, perhaps merely unconscious people, so he revived Sam, dead for over four thousand years; Sam called him a prophet, some believed, and others called it magic and demanded a sign.
rows.anchor: إنك تحي من كان قريب العهد من الموت ولعلهم لم يموتوا بل أصابتهم سكتة فأحي لنا سام بن نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports say Isa revived a king's son to succeed him and also revived a fawn, sheep, and cow.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد أيضا أنه عليه السلام أحيا ابن ملك ليستخلفه في قصة طويلة وأحيا خشفا وشاة وبقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word الموتى encompasses all of these reported cases.
rows.anchor: ولفظ ( الموتى ) يعم كل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in both clauses is either a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun described by a clause, with its pronoun omitted; the house phrase modifies its verb, with no تنازع.
rows.anchor: ( ما ) في الموضعين موصولة أو نكرة موصوفة والعائد محذوف أي تأكلونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ادخار means hiding or storing something away.
rows.anchor: والادخار الخبء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying form is تذتخرون; its ta changes to dhal, then dhal to dal and assimilates, with some Arabs instead changing ta to dal and assimilating.
rows.anchor: ( وأصل ) تدخرون تذتخرون بذال معجمة فتاء فأبدلت التاء ذالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports place Isa's foretelling after his prophethood and reviving the dead.
rows.anchor: وقد كان هذا الإخبار بعد النبوة وإحيائه الموتى عليه السلام على ما في بعض الأخبار

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Ibn Asakir transmits from Abdullah ibn Amr that as a boy Isa told playmates what their mothers had hidden for them; when the boys checked, their mothers asked who had informed them, and they named Isa.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن عساكر عن عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص أنه قال : كان عيسى عليه السلام وهو غلام

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: In the same account, people feared Isa would influence the boys, shut them in a house, and answered his inquiry by saying they were monkeys and pigs; he prayed that they become so, and they did.
rows.anchor: فجمعوهم في بيت وأغلقوه عليهم فخرج عيسى يلتمسهم فلم يجدهم حتى سمع ضوضاهم في بيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places the foretelling after the descent of the table.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعضهم أن ذلك كان بعد نزول المائدة

rows.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
rows.claim: Abd al-Razzaq and others transmit Ammar ibn Yasir's explanation that the foretelling concerned food from the table; people were told to eat and not store any, but some stored food and betrayed the condition, becoming apes and pigs.
rows.anchor: وأيد بما أخرجه عبدالرزاق وغيره عن عمار بن ياسر رضي الله تعالى عنه في الآية أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi allows that both accounts could have occurred; in any case, the apparent sense is that Isa foretold these two particular matters.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : إن كل ذلك قد وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the examples as representative of all unseen matters; specifying familiar personal facts leaves the hearers no room to doubt.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد الاخبار بالمغيبات إلا أنه قد اقتصر على ذكر أمرين منها ولعل وجه تخصيص الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food and stored provisions are singled out because people devote much effort to obtaining nourishment and feel reassured by having reserves.
rows.anchor: والسر في ذكر هذين الامرين بخصوصهما أن غالب سعى الانسان وصرف ذهنه لتحصيل الأكل الذي به قوامه والادخار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads تدخرون with dhal and without gemination.
rows.anchor: وقرئ تدخرون بالذال المعجمة والتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك refers to the four extraordinary signs just mentioned.
rows.anchor: أي المذكور من الخوارق الأربعة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement may be Isa's speech as reported by God, or God's own words spoken as rebuke.
rows.anchor: وهذا من كلام عيسى عليه السلام حكاه الله تعالى عنه وقيل : هو من كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular آية may denote a genus; another reading has the plural لآيات.
rows.anchor: لآية ( أي جنسها وقرئ لآيات لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs clearly establish the messenger's truth because they occur without instruments or ordinary causes used by physicians and astrologers.
rows.anchor: دالة على صحة الرسالة دلالة واضحة حيث لم يكن ذلك بتخلل آلات وتوسط أسباب عادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jafr, astrology, and similar disciplined arts are not knowledge of the unseen: they depend on known principles and cosmic means; some say they yield only strong probability, far from certain unseen knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم أن علم الجفر وعلم الفلك ونحوهما لما كانت مقرونة بأصول وضوابط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelatory knowledge is not acquired but granted by God; inspiration likewise has no material basis, only divine bestowal.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك كالعلم بالوحي لأنه غير مكتسب بل الله تعالى يختص به من يشاء وكذا العلم بالإلهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional may mean if you are enabled to believe, or if you believe; in either case the omitted result is that you benefit from the sign.
rows.anchor: فيه مجاز المشارقة أي إن كنتم موفقين للايمان ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى إن كنتم مصدقين وجواب الشرط على التقديرين محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This new instruction follows counsel to spouses on kind treatment and resolving discord; it reinforces marital rights and teaches good dealings with all classes of people.
rows.anchor: مسوق للإرشاد إلى خلال مشتملة على معالي الأمور إثر إرشاد كل من الزوجين إلى المعاملة الحسنة وإزالة الخصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's rights are placed first because they are the greatest foundation; that order also signals the high standing of the duties listed after them.
rows.anchor: وقدم الأمر بما يتعلق بحقوق الله تعالى لأنها المدار الأعظم وفي ذلك إيماء أيضا إلى ارتفاع شأن ما نظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is the utmost degree of submission.
rows.anchor: والعبادة أقصى غاية الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شيئا may be a direct object, with indefinite tanwin generalizing the prohibition to anything whatsoever, idol or otherwise.
rows.anchor: و ( شيئا ) إما مفعول به أي لا تشركوا به شيئا من الأشياء

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: Isam al-Din takes the tanwin as belittling: associating even a contemptible thing with God's limitless greatness merits severe rebuke.
rows.anchor: واختار عصام الدين كونه للتحقير ليكون فيه توبيخ عظيم أي لا تشركوا به شيئا حقيرا

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: He argues that relating a contingent being to the Necessary is more remote than relating nonexistence to existence, since nonexistence is the possibility of existence.
rows.anchor: ونسب الممكن إلى الواجب أبعد من نسبة المعدوم إلى الموجود إذ المعدوم إمكان الموجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively شيئا is a verbal noun: associate nothing with God, whether openly or secretly.
rows.anchor: وإما مصدر أي لا تشركوا به عز شأنه من الإشراك جليا أو خفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban may follow because worship as total submission cannot be directed to one who has a partner, or to rebuke people for missing that implication.
rows.anchor: للنهي عن الإشراك فيما جعله الشرع علامة نهاية الخضوع أو للتوبيخ بغاية الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the clearer reading is that the prohibition commands sincerity, restating worship as worshipping God alone.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأوضح أن يقال : إن هذا النهي إشارة إلى الأمر بالإخلاص

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam explains the sequence as a general command covering heart and bodily acts followed by its specific core, monotheism, without which God accepts no deed; it is coordination of the specific with the general.
rows.anchor: إلى أن سبحانه أمر أولا بما يشمل التوحيد وغيره من أعمال القلب والجوارح ثم أردفه بما يفهم منه التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means and treat both parents well: the preposition may modify an omitted verb or the verbal noun; it is fronted for emphasis.
rows.anchor: أي وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا فالجار متعلق بالفعل المقدر وجوز تعلقه بالمصدر وقدم للاهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحسن takes باء, إلى, or لام; one view allows باء only when the verb conveys affection.
rows.anchor: وأحسن يتعدى بالباء وإلى واللام وقيل : إنما يتعدى بالباء إذا تضمن معنى العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness includes serving parents, not raising one's voice or speaking harshly, meeting their needs, and supporting them within one's means.
rows.anchor: أن يقوم بخدمتهما ولا يرفع صوته عليهما ولا يخشن في الكلام معهما ويسعى في تحصيل مطالبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذو القربى means a relative, such as a brother, uncle, maternal uncle, or their children.
rows.anchor: أي بصاحب القرابة من أخ وعو وخال وأولاد كل نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition is repeated here, unlike al-Baqara, because this is counsel to this community and is therefore emphasized; the earlier instruction addressed the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وأعيد الباء هنا ولم يعد في البقرة قال في البحر : لأن هذا توصية لهذه الأمة فاعتني به وأكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphans and poor in this phrase are those outside one's family.
rows.anchor: واليتمى والمسكين ( من الأجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of near neighbor is a neighbor close by location.
rows.anchor: أي الذي قرب جواره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, near neighbor is also connected by kinship or religion, while the distant neighbor has no kinship or is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالجار ذي القربى من له مع الجوار قرب واتصال بنسب أو دين

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبدالله
rows.claim: A report through Abu Nuaym and al-Bazzar, which al-Alusi says is weak, assigns three rights to the kin Muslim neighbor, two to a Muslim neighbor without kinship, and one to a non-Muslim neighbor from the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو نعيم والبزار من حديث جابر بن عبدالله وفيه ضعف قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari's Adab collection reports Ibn Umar repeatedly telling his servant to give meat to their Jewish neighbor, citing the Prophet's teaching that Gabriel kept urging care for neighbors until he thought they would inherit.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البخاري في الأدب عن عبدالله بن عمر أنه ذبحت له شاة فجعل يقول لغلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The customary understanding of neighborhood determines who counts as a neighbor.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن مبنى الجوار على العرف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan defines a neighbor as extending forty houses in front, behind, to the right, and to the left; a similar report is attributed to al-Zuhri.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن كما في الأدب أنه سئل عن الجار فقال : أربعين دارا أمامه وأربعين خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view defines the neighbor's distance as forty cubits.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أربعين ذراعا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha asked which of two neighbors should receive a gift; the Prophet said to choose the one whose door is nearer.
rows.anchor: فعن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : قلت : يا رسول الله إن لي جارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads الجار ذي القربى in the accusative, meaning and I single out the near neighbor, highlighting the neighbor's right.
rows.anchor: وقرئ والجار ذي القربى بالنصب أي وأخص الجار وفي ذلك تنبيه على عظم حق الجار

rows.speaker: أبو شريح الخزاعي
rows.claim: The two Sahih collections transmit Abu Shurayh's report from the Prophet: whoever believes in God and the Last Day should treat his neighbor well.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرج الشيخان عن أبي شريح الخزاعي أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : من كان يؤمن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for two meanings of the companion at one's side: a travel companion or someone who relies on you and seeks your aid.
rows.anchor: وهو الرفيق في السفر أو المنقطع إليك يرجو نفعك ورفدك وكلا القولين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a companion in a good undertaking such as learning, trade, a craft, or travel; some include anyone who sits beside one in a mosque, gathering, or other brief companionship, a view praised for its breadth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الرفيق في أمر حسن كتعلم وتصرف وصناعة وسفر وعدوا من ذلك من قعد بجنبك في مسجد

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says the companion at one's side is one's wife.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه الصاحب بالجنب المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element serving as a circumstantial modifier of الصاحب, governed by the estimated verb.
rows.anchor: والجار متعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من الصاحب والعامل فيه الفعل المقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-sabil means a traveler or guest.
rows.anchor: وهو المسافر أو الضيف

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies those possessed by the right hand as male and female slaves.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : من عبيدكم وإمائكم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Ahmad and al-Bayhaqi transmit from Anas that the Prophet's final counsel repeatedly included prayer and those under one's authority, even as his speech failed near death.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج أحمد والبيهقي عن أنس قال : كان عامة وصية رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم حين حضره الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required degree of kindness to these various groups differs according to what suits each one.
rows.anchor: ثم الإحسان إلى هؤلاء الأصناف متفاوت المراتب حسبما يليق بكل وينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhtal means arrogant and conceited, disdaining relatives and neighbors and ignoring them.
rows.anchor: أي ذا خيلاء وكبر يأنف من أقاربه وجيرانه مثلا ولا يلتفت إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakhur is someone who vaunts his merits over others with pride.
rows.anchor: يعد مناقبه عليهم تطاولا وتعاظما

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالًۭا فَخُورًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that God does not love the arrogant explains the preceding commands to kindness.
rows.anchor: والجملة تعليل للأمر السابق

rows.speaker: ثابت بن قيس بن شماس
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh report that Thabit ibn Qays wept after hearing the verse and fearing its warning; he loved fine appearance, even in his sandal strap. The Prophet reassured him that beautifying one's mount and belongings is not arrogance, which is rejecting truth and belittling people.
rows.anchor: أخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه عن ثابت بن قيس بن شماس قال : كنت عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage resumes to explain the terrible state whose severity was just indicated.
rows.anchor: استئناف لبيان حالهم التي أشير إلى شدتها وفظاعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nunation of إذ may stand in place of the two preceding clauses, the first clause alone, or the last clause alone.
rows.anchor: وتنوين إذ عوض على الصحيح عن الجملتين السابقتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal phrase modifies يود; taking it with شهيد and making يود its adjective, with a deleted resumptive pronoun, is remote.
rows.anchor: والظرف متعلق بيود وجعله متعلقا بشهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative may refer specifically to those who denied the Messenger; the wording rebukes them and marks the cause of their dreadful state.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عنهم بذلك لذمهم بما في حيز الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad the Messenger honors him and further condemns those who deny him.
rows.anchor: وإيراده صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بعنوان الرسالة لتشريفه وزيادة تقبيح حال مكذبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means disbelievers generally, especially those who denied the Prophet; رسول is also generic but chiefly includes Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وإما جنس الكفرة ويدخل أولئك في زمرتهم دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عصوا is coordinated with كفروا within the relative clause and refers to disobedience beyond disbelief, implying that disbelievers are accountable for derivative duties.
rows.anchor: داخل معه في حيز الصلة والمراد عصيانهم بما سوى الكفر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa instead parses عصوا as a circumstantial clause attached to the subject of كفروا, with قد understood.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : إنه في موضع الحال من ضمير ( كفروا )

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Another analysis treats this as two coordinated relatives, describing two groups, which works on al-Farra's view that a relative pronoun can be elided.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صلة لموصول آخر أي والذين عصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day, the people described from their worldly state wish for this because the day brings added severity and doubled terror.
rows.anchor: أي يود في ذلك اليوم لمزيد شدته ومضاعف هوله الموصوفون بما ذكر في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One syntax makes the لو clause the object of يود, with لو meaning that; they wish to be buried and the earth leveled over them like the dead.
rows.anchor: إما مفعول ( يود ) على أن ( لو ) مصدرية أي يودون أن يدفنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they wish they had remained dust as they originally were, never created.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يودون أنهم بقوا ترابا على أصلهم من غير خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that animals become dust and the unbelievers wish they shared that fate.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تصير البهائم ترابا فيودون حالها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they wish the gathered people would walk over them, treading them as they tread the ground.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المعنى يودون أن يمشى عليهم أهل الجمع يطأونهم بأقدامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as wishing to be exchanged for the earth, giving everything on it as ransom.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يودون لو يعدل بهم الأرض أي يؤخذ منهم ما عليها فدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, لو retains its usual conditional sense; يود has an omitted object and the conditional answer is also omitted, understood from the context.
rows.anchor: وإما مستأنفة على أن ( لو ) على بابها ومفعول ( يود ) محذوف

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر ويزيد
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Yazid read تسوى as تتسوى with the first ta assimilated into the nearby sin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر ويزيد ( تسوى ) على أن أصله تتسوى

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read تسوى by dropping the second ta and applying imala.
rows.anchor: وحمزة والكسائي ( تسوى ) بحذف التاء الثانية مع الإمالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may be unable to conceal anything because their limbs testify against them; or they admit all their deeds, knowing concealment will not help, despite saying at some points that they were not polytheists.
rows.anchor: لا يكتمون من الله تعالى حديثا لعدم قدرتهم على الكتمان حيث أن جوارحهم تشهد عليهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains that they confess because they know concealment cannot benefit them, though in some situations they say they were not polytheists.
rows.anchor: وإنما لا يكتمون لعلمهم بأنهم لا ينفعهم الكتمان وإنما يقولون : ( والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين )

words: يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the waw is circumstantial: they wish to be buried while not concealing anything or denying the truth with the claim that they were not polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الواو للحال أي يودون أن يدفنوا في الأرض وهم لا يكتمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Hakim, whose report al-Alusi says is authentic, transmits from Ibn Abbas that after they deny being polytheists, God seals their mouths and their limbs testify, making them wish the earth were leveled over them.
rows.anchor: إذ روى الحاكم وصححه عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم إذا قالوا ذلك ختم الله على أفواههم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Attribution of what follows to تسوى is judged very remote: the wish would be that they had not concealed Muhammad and his sending in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وجعلها للعطف وما بعدها معطوف على ( تسوى ) على معنى يودون لو تسوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi calls that coordination very remote; a closer analysis coordinates non-concealment with the object of يود, expressing a wish for the earth's leveling and for their having concealed nothing.
rows.anchor: بعيد جدا وأقرب منه العطف على مفعول ( يود ) على معنى يودون تسوية الأرض بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative coordination is understood against their statement that they were not polytheists.
rows.anchor: إذ قالوا ( والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين )
